```{python}
from research_site import Study

study = Study()
VERSE = "Verse-level"
PASSAGE = "Passage-level"
```

## Summary

- We fine-tuned two other pretrained models, MADLAD and T5Gemma, on the same data as an NLLB baseline for one low-resource language.
- **NLLB scored highest.** MADLAD with verse-level training reached 61.8 passage-level chrF3 against NLLB's 66.7. T5Gemma reached about 44.
- **Training and translating whole passages was worse than single verses** for both alternatives.

## The question

Our NLLB experiments use one verse at a time, and the [combining-verses study](../2026-11-combining-verses/index.html) found that joining verses did not help. Other pretrained models may handle longer inputs or translate better. This study asks whether MADLAD or T5Gemma beats NLLB on the same task.

## How it was tested

- **Language and data.** Language O (the label used in [combining verses](../2026-11-combining-verses/index.html)), translated from a related language of wider communication. All models were trained on the whole New Testament except Matthew 11-16, which is the test set. NLLB has no passage-level run here. Scores are passage-level chrF3.
- **Models.** NLLB is the baseline from the earlier studies. MADLAD and T5Gemma were fine-tuned with silnlp.
- **Verse-level or passage-level.** Verse-level runs train and translate one verse at a time. Passage-level runs train and translate whole passages; for T5Gemma the context window was 1,000 tokens.
- **Epochs.** T5Gemma was trained for 100 and for 1,000 epochs at verse level.

## Results

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
study.dot_chart(
    "Passage-level chrF3",
    groups=[VERSE, PASSAGE],
    x_title="Passage-level chrF3 (Matthew 11-16)",
)
```

```{python}
study.table(groups=[VERSE, PASSAGE], group_title="Training and translating", intervals=False)
```

- **MADLAD is 4.9 points below NLLB at verse level**, and 17.8 below it at passage level.
- **T5Gemma is about 22 points below NLLB at verse level.** Ten times the epochs added 0.6 points, so training length does not explain the gap.
- **Passage-level training cost 12.9 points for MADLAD and 10.8 for T5Gemma.** We don't know why. Long passages may be truncated, as in the [combining-verses study](../2026-11-combining-verses/index.html).
- **Cost.** MADLAD did not fit on A100 GPUs or on half of an H100; it needed a full 94 GB H100. T5Gemma ran on half of an H100 (we did not try A100s).

<!-- REVIEW: the takeaways and the 'long passages may be truncated' hypothesis are the drafter's reading of the slide numbers; Laura confirmed them in conversation, a second reader should check. GPU notes come from slide text, not a results file. -->

## Limitations

- **One run per setting and no intervals.** Differences within about a point of chrF3 are not established, including 100 against 1,000 epochs.
- **One language and one test set**, six chapters of Matthew.
- **Settings were not tuned per model.** The models may need different hyperparameters than NLLB, so this is a comparison of defaults, not of best possible results.
